main_diagnosis: The simulator is missing a slow non-inactivating potassium channel (M-current, Kv7/KCNQ). All additional channel slots (X1, X2) are extracted but never used in the current dynamics. This causes: (1) incorrect spike count (mse_per_dim[0]=2.22) because there is no spike-frequency adaptation or rate-limiting slow K+ current, and (2) excessive subthreshold voltage variability (mse_per_dim[2]=3.16 for resting std) because without a slowly-activating stabilizing conductance the membrane is too sensitive to noise near rest. The elevated variance (1.34) and skewness (1.23) during stimulation also point to missing inter-spike interval regulation.

issues.description: No additional channel is implemented despite X1/X2 conductance parameters being extracted. The M-current (slow, non-inactivating K+ current) is the most parsimonious fix: it activates at subthreshold voltages, does not inactivate, reduces firing rate via adaptation, and damps subthreshold oscillations — directly addressing the high spike-count MSE and high resting-potential STD MSE.
issues.location: All '# BEGIN EDITABLE SECTION' blocks in forward(). Specifically: kinetics definition block, state variable declaration, initialization, simulation loop (alpha/beta computation, tau_V_inv, V_inf, state update).

issues.description: The standard deviation of the resting potential (mse_per_dim[2]=3.16) is the single largest error dimension, indicating subthreshold membrane instability. With no slow stabilizing conductance, the noise term (nois_fact) perturbs the membrane without an effective restoring force, causing excessive voltage fluctuations at rest.
issues.location: tau_V_inv and V_inf computation inside the simulation loop.
issues.suggestion: Once the M-current gating variable p is added (see issue 1), its contribution gbar_X1 * p[:, i-1] in tau_V_inv will increase the effective membrane conductance at rest, shortening the membrane time constant and reducing sensitivity to noise. This directly reduces resting potential standard deviation. Ensure param_i is in a subthreshold range (e.g., ~-35 mV, which corresponds to params[:,8] ~ 35) so p is partially activated at rest and provides tonic stabilizing outward current.
